newsitem.title: USA: KC Fed's Hoenig says U.S. economy in good shape.
newsitem.headline: KC Fed's Hoenig says U.S. economy in good shape.

text.p: President of the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Thomas Hoenig said the U.S. economy is performing well across the board, but highlighted the central bank's dilemma on inflation.

Addressing a seminar sponsored by the Missouri State Treasurer here on Thursday, he said, "It's a pleasure to be talking about the economy since it is uniformly very good everywhere I've gone in the country. It is a strong economy doing very well."
Still, Hoenig said, in the second quarter American consumers took a breather and slowed spending somewhat, although businesses appear to have "picked up the slack."
Also, Hoenig said, in the second quarter the inventory-to-sales ratio remained very modest, manufacturing continued to grow and residential investment remained resilient.
"The one sector that appears somewhat sluggish right now is of course the export (sector) where the strong dollar and the sluggish growth abroad has softened demand for our goods," Hoenig said.

Turning to inflation, Hoenig said despite strong economic growth, the U.S. has been fortunate that price pressures have remained moderate. But, he said, while inflation trends have been favorable, central bankers still need to be cautious about inflation.
"The critical issue is whether the strong growth in demand will be matched by continued strong growth in supply. If not, demand outstrips supply and we will have increased inflation."
Helping the low-inflation scenario, Hoeing said, was a strong U.S. dollar.

As from where inflation might rear its ugly head in the future, the Kansas City Fed president said labor benefit costs bear watching. In addition, he pointed to upside risk on inflation given the historically low unemployment rate.
"There is some upside risk when you look at that very favorable employment rate," he said.
Finally, Hoenig said the central bank faced a dilemma in the current inflation environment.
"You don't want to act too soon, but you also don't want to wait too long, so you watch these numbers very carefully," he said.
